title: WPSS/626/2021 of BHAGWATI BHATT Vs GOVERNMENT OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH ITS SECRETARY MEDICAL DEHRADUN

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.626 of 2021
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. Atul Bahuguna, Standing Counsel
for the State/respondent nos. 1 and 2.
Mr. Nishant Krishna Adhikari,
Advocate holding brief of Mr. Ramji
Shrivastava, Advocate for the respondent
no.3.
It is the case of the petitioners that
they applied to the post of X-Ray
Technician pursuant to the advertisement
dated 28.05.2017, issued by Uttarakhand
Subordinate Service Selection Commission.
They appeared in the examination and were
selected. Their names find place in the
merit list, but their names were not
recommended by the recruiting agency on
the ground that the petitioners were not
registered with the Uttarakhand Para-medical Council.
It has been the case of the petitioners
that they did apply for their registration
with the Uttarakhand Para-medical
Council, but it is the Council, who failed to
register them with promptitude. Therefore,
it is the claim of the petitioners that non-recommending of their names for
appointment is not as per law.
Subsequently, the candidature of the
petitioners were rejected by the order dated
24.05.2018, which was challenged by the
petitioners in WPSS 1552 of 2018, WPSS
No.1704 of 2018, WPSS No.1705 of 2018,
WPSS No.1706 of 2018 and WPSS No.1469
of 2018, which were pending for final
hearing. In the meanwhile, the respondent

no.3, the Uttarakhand Medical Service
Selection Board, issued fresh advertisement
on 13.05.2021, to fill up the posts.
The instant petition has been filed for
quashing the advertisement dated
13.05.2021, issued by the respondent no.3,
the Uttarakhand Medical Service Selection
Board. Counter affidavit has been filed.
Today, learned counsel for the
petitioners would submit that since in view
of the earlier writ petitions filed by the
petitioners and others, 9 posts have already
been kept vacant by the Medical Health and
Family Welfare Department, no purpose
would be served to continue with the writ
petition. He would refer to Para 4 of the
counter affidavit filed by Smt. Garima
Rounkaly, Secretary Uttarakhand Medical
Service Selection Board, in which it is
stated that after rejection of the petitioners'
representation dated 24.05.2018, they filed
writ petitions and pursuant to it, it is stated
that, "It is submitted here that the
Medical Health and Family Welfare
Department has already kept vacant 9
posts of X-Ray Technician, which are
subject to the final decision of the writ
petitions pending before this Court."
Learned counsel for the respondent
no.3 would submit that 9 posts are kept
vacant, but he would submit that for
petitioners, only 2 posts have been kept
vacant. The Court wanted to know as to
why other 7 posts have been kept vacant?
Learned counsel for the respondent no.3
would submit that there are other writ
petitions also.
Learned counsel for the respondent
nos. 1 and 2 would submit that 5 posts are
kept vacant, which belong to backlog.

has stated that since 9 posts have already
been kept vacant by the respondent nos. 1
and 2, no purpose would be served to
continue with the writ petition.
In view of what is stated hereinabove,
this Court is of the view that nothing
survives in this writ petition. It stands
disposed of, accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani J.)
12.07.2023
